title: The dressing-room mirror
body: Riya, who is 1.6 m tall with her eyes 1.5 m above the floor, stands 2 m in front of a vertical plane mirror fixed on the wall of a dressing room. She then walks straight towards the mirror at a steady speed of 0.5 m/s for 2 s. The floor is level and the mirror is vertical.

title: Laws of reflection at a science exhibition
body: At a science exhibition, students fix a plane mirror vertically at the edge of a chart paper laid flat on a table. They draw the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence and mark angles with a protractor. A laser pointer kept flat on the chart sends a narrow beam towards the mirror at an angle of incidence of 40°, and the path of the reflected beam is traced on the chart.

title: A school solar cooker
body: A village school builds a solar cooker using a polished concave reflector whose radius of curvature is 1.2 m. The reflector is turned so that its principal axis points straight at the Sun. The students must decide where to keep the cooking pot so that the food cooks fastest.

title: The torch reflector
body: A torch has a small bulb fixed in front of a concave reflector of focal length 3 cm. When the bulb is exactly at the principal focus, the torch sends out a beam whose width does not change with distance. A repair mechanic tests what happens when the bulb holder slips a little forward or backward along the principal axis.

title: The truck in the rear-view mirror
body: A car's rear-view mirror is a convex mirror with a radius of curvature of 4.0 m. A truck 3.0 m high is 6.0 m behind the mirror and is slowly coming closer. Use the New Cartesian sign convention, the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = h'/h = −v/u.

title: The dentist's mirror
body: A dentist uses a small concave mirror of focal length 4.0 cm to examine a cavity. She first holds the mirror so that the tooth is 2.0 cm from it, and then moves it until the tooth is 3.0 cm away. Use the New Cartesian sign convention, 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = −v/u.

title: Tracing a ray through a glass slab
body: In a school laboratory, a student traces the path of a ray through a rectangular glass slab placed on a sheet of paper. For an angle of incidence of 40° at the first face, she measures the angle of refraction inside the slab as 25°. (sin 40° = 0.643, sin 25° = 0.423)

title: Spear fishing
body: A fisherman standing on the bank of a clear, still pond sees a fish below the water surface. He wants to hit it with a spear thrown in a straight line from his eye level. His friend warns him that the fish is not where it appears to be.

title: A table of refractive indices
body: A student copies these absolute refractive indices from a data table: water 1.33, ethyl alcohol 1.36, kerosene 1.44, crown glass 1.52, diamond 2.42. The speed of light in vacuum is c = 3 × 10^8 m/s.

title: Speed of light in three liquids
body: In a virtual laboratory, a student measures the speed of light in three transparent liquids: Liquid P: 2.25 × 10^8 m/s, Liquid Q: 2.0 × 10^8 m/s and Liquid R: 2.4 × 10^8 m/s. The speed of light in vacuum is c = 3 × 10^8 m/s.

title: The slide projector
body: A school uses an old slide projector. A transparent slide is placed in front of a convex projection lens, and a sharp, enlarged picture is obtained on a screen several metres away on the other side of the lens. The operator always inserts the slides upside down.

title: Candle, lens and screen
body: A student places a lit candle 25 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm and moves a screen on the other side of the lens until a sharp image of the flame appears on it.

title: An optician's prescription
body: An optician's prescription reads: Right lens −1.5 D, Left lens +2.0 D. The power of a lens is P = 1/f, with f in metres; for lenses in contact, P = P1 + P2.

title: Finding the focal length by the u–v method
body: In a laboratory experiment to find the focal length of a convex lens, a student records: object at 30 cm from the lens → sharp image at 60 cm on the other side; object at 40 cm → sharp image at 40 cm on the other side. Use the New Cartesian sign convention, 1/v − 1/u = 1/f and m = v/u.
